```plato
//==
// # Planar
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Rounded-rectangle, oriented-box, and regular-polygon bodies
//  - Disk, annulus, sector, segment, and stadium bodies
//  - Ellipse and superellipse bodies
//  - Local-frame and centred-bounds helpers
//  - Triangle, quadrilateral, and parallelogram bodies

library Planar
{
    //==
    // # Rounded-rectangle, oriented-box, and regular-polygon bodies
    //
    // Area, perimeter, bounds, centroid, containment, nearest-point and support bodies
    // for the types declared in `planar.types.plato`.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here:
    //
    //   * PLACED, not origin-centred, and SIZES ARE FULL EXTENTS, so every body halves
    //     them.
    //   * `Area` is non-negative for EVERY type here.
    //   * CONTAINMENT is boundary-INCLUSIVE wherever the test is an inequality on a
    //     distance or a coordinate. The even-odd test (RegularPolygon) cannot honour
    //     that: a point exactly on an edge falls whichever way the floating point
    //     comparison goes.
    //   * `ClosestPoint` on a filled REGION returns the query point itself when the
    //     query is contained, which `INearestPoint2D` explicitly permits.
    //   * ANGLES are `Angle` throughout; `Number` fractions of a turn are converted with
    //     `.Turns` (`angles.library.plato`) rather than by multiplying by pi.
    //
    // Shared kernels live in `geometry.library.plato` and the local-frame
    // helpers in `lines.library.plato`; neither is respelled here.

    //==
    // # RoundedRect2D
    //
    // An axis-aligned rectangle Minkowski-summed with a disk of the corner radius
    // (equivalently: the rectangle with its four corners replaced by quarter arcs).

    // CornerRadius clamped to the declaration's stated range: never negative, never
    // more than half the smaller side. Every body below reads this, not the raw
    // field, so an out-of-range stored value degrades gracefully.
    EffectiveCornerRadius(r: RoundedRect2D): Number
        => r.CornerRadius.Clamp(0.0, r.Rect.Size.Width.Min(r.Rect.Size.Height) * 0.5);

    // w*h minus the four corner offcuts: each corner replaces an r-by-r square with
    // a quarter disk, removing (4 - pi) * r^2 in total.
    Area(r: RoundedRect2D): Number
    {
        var radius = r.EffectiveCornerRadius;
        return r.Rect.Size.Width * r.Rect.Size.Height - (4.0 - Number.Pi) * radius.Square;
    }

    // The four straight runs (2(w + h) - 8r) plus the four quarter arcs (2*pi*r).
    Perimeter(r: RoundedRect2D): Number
    {
        var radius = r.EffectiveCornerRadius;
        return 2.0 * (r.Rect.Size.Width + r.Rect.Size.Height)
            - 8.0 * radius + 2.0 * Number.Pi * radius;
    }

    // The rectangle's centre: the rounding is symmetric in both axes.
    Centroid(r: RoundedRect2D): Point2D
        => r.Rect.Center;

    // The underlying rectangle — the rounded shape touches all four sides, so this
    // is tight.
    Bounds(r: RoundedRect2D): Bounds2D
        => CenteredBounds(r.Rect.Center, r.Rect.Size.Width * 0.5, r.Rect.Size.Height * 0.5);

    // The standard rounded-box inside test: fold the query into the first quadrant,
    // subtract the inner (unrounded) half-extents, and compare the resulting
    // distance to the corner radius. Boundary inclusive.
    // https://iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d/
    Contains(r: RoundedRect2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var radius = r.EffectiveCornerRadius;
        var qx = (point.X - r.Rect.Center.X).Abs - (r.Rect.Size.Width * 0.5 - radius);
        var qy = (point.Y - r.Rect.Center.Y).Abs - (r.Rect.Size.Height * 0.5 - radius);
        var outside = (qx.Max(0.0).Square + qy.Max(0.0).Square).Sqrt;
        return outside + qx.Max(qy).Min(0.0) <= radius;
    }

    //==
    // # OrientedBox2D
    //
    // A rectangle with arbitrary rotation. Size is the FULL width and height, so
    // every body halves it. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_bounding_box

    // Width times height; rotation does not change area.
    Area(b: OrientedBox2D): Number
        => b.Size.Width * b.Size.Height;

    // Twice the sum of the side lengths.
    Perimeter(b: OrientedBox2D): Number
        => 2.0 * (b.Size.Width + b.Size.Height);


    // TIGHT bounds of a rotated rectangle: the half-extent along each world axis is
    // the sum of the two local half-extents weighted by |cos| and |sin| — the
    // support function of the box evaluated on that axis.
    Bounds(b: OrientedBox2D): Bounds2D
    {
        var c = b.Rotation.Cos.Abs;
        var s = b.Rotation.Sin.Abs;
        var hx = b.Size.Width * 0.5;
        var hy = b.Size.Height * 0.5;
        return CenteredBounds(b.Center, hx * c + hy * s, hx * s + hy * c);
    }

    // True when the query, expressed in the box's own frame, lies within the
    // half-extents on both axes. Boundary inclusive.
    Contains(b: OrientedBox2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var q = LocalOffset(b.Center, b.Rotation, point);
        return q.X.Abs <= b.Size.Width * 0.5 && q.Y.Abs <= b.Size.Height * 0.5;
    }

    // The query point when it is inside, otherwise the query clamped to the box in
    // the box's own frame and mapped back to world.
    ClosestPoint(b: OrientedBox2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
    {
        var hx = b.Size.Width * 0.5;
        var hy = b.Size.Height * 0.5;
        var q = LocalOffset(b.Center, b.Rotation, point);
        var clamped = Vector2D(q.X.Clamp(-hx, hx), q.Y.Clamp(-hy, hy));
        return b.Contains(point) ? point : b.Center + WorldOffset(b.Rotation, clamped);
    }

    // The corner of the box farthest along `direction`: each local axis
    // independently takes the sign of the direction's component on it.
    Support(b: OrientedBox2D, direction: Direction2D): Point2D
    {
        var d = LocalOffset(b.Center, b.Rotation, b.Center + direction.Vector);
        var hx = b.Size.Width * 0.5;
        var hy = b.Size.Height * 0.5;
        return b.Center + WorldOffset(b.Rotation,
            Vector2D(d.X >= 0.0 ? hx : -hx, d.Y >= 0.0 ? hy : -hy));
    }

    //==
    // # RegularPolygon
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_polygon

    // The SideCount vertices on the circumscribed circle, counter-clockwise from
    // Rotation. Named distinctly from `Points` because RegularPolygon does not
    // implement IPointSet2D — its vertices are computed, not stored.
    RegularPolygonVertices(g: RegularPolygon): Array<Point2D>
        => g.SideCount.MapRange(i =>
        {
            var a = g.Rotation + (i.ToNumber / g.SideCount.ToNumber).Turns;
            return g.Center + Vector2D(a.Cos, a.Sin) * g.CircumRadius;
        });
```
